properties.bedrock_geology: Inverclyde Group and Strathclyde Group (Carboniferous Sandstone, Siltstone, and Mudstone sequence)
properties.fluvial_geomorphology: Incised river gorge carved by the Water of Leith through glacial till and sedimentary strata
properties.soil_profile: Alluvial silts, dark humic loam over glacial boulder clay and rocky riverbank debris
properties.hydrology: Water of Leith riverbed at approximately 12–15m above sea level, subject to natural urban-rural catchment runoff

structures.name: St Bernard's Well Pumphouse (Neoclassical Rotunda / Temple)
structures.architectural_style: Neoclassical Doric circular temple (Alexander Nasmyth design, 1789)

materials.dome: Lead-covered shallow dome surmounted by a pineapple finial
materials.interior_statue: Marble statue of Hygieia (Goddess of Health)

materials.walls: Coursed rubble sandstone with dressed coping stones
materials.pavement: Compacted gravel and stone slab walkways along the Water of Leith Walkway

properties.vegetation: Mature canopy of weeping willows, sycamores, beech, and alder flanking the river gorge; mosses, liverworts, and ferns lining wet sandstone river walls
properties.atmosphere: Cool Scottish valley microclimate, morning river mist clearing, filtered northern daylight (5200K) casting soft raking beams through dense overhanging deciduous foliage
